prompt:
Scope (frontend-only): implement all client-side changes required so the UI and client code (requests and response processing) stop relying on a response field named "title". Ensure the client no longer sends a "title" property in any request payload. Do not change any backend or database fields.

Preserved API facts and constraints (must be explicitly satisfied and verified by frontend changes/tests):
- Public responses will no longer include a "title" attribute for entries; responses must be consumed using the "name" attribute only.
- Requests that include a "title" field will continue to be rejected with HTTP 422. The frontend must stop sending "title" in requests.
- Database column names are NOT changing. Do not attempt to rename or refer to DB fields in frontend code; treat persistence details as unchanged.
- The other response fields remain unchanged and must continue to be used as before: description, id, owner_id, created_at.

Implementation tasks (step-by-step):
1) Audit codebase for all usages of "title":
   - Search for the exact tokens: title, .title, ["title"], 'title' in code, tests, fixtures, and storybook/mocks.
   - Search places to include: components, containers, hooks, services/api clients, serializers/adapters, TypeScript interfaces/types, GraphQL/REST query mappers, form components, validation code, unit/e2e tests, mocks, storybook stories, fixtures, analytics/tracking, and docs in the repo.
   - Record every file that reads or writes a "title" property.

2) Remove fallback logic that reads title from all response handling and UI rendering:
   - Replace code patterns like: item.name || item.title or get(item, 'title') as a fallback with strict usage of item.name only.
   - Where UI previously displayed title when name missing, change behavior to: show name if present; if name is missing, show a clear placeholder (e.g., "(no name)") or an explicit empty-state UI. Do not attempt to read title.
   - Update any helper functions, renderers, and localization lookups that used title as a fallback.

3) Stop sending "title" in outbound requests:
   - Update API client serializers/adapters to omit title from request bodies for create and update endpoints. Either remove assignment of title in payload construction or explicitly delete payload.title before sending.
   - Update form handlers and DTO builders so they do not include a title key. If the UI previously had a Title input field, change it to bind to "name" instead or remove it; ensure the network payload uses only name for the entity label.
   - If any middleware or interceptors automatically copy client-side fields into requests (e.g., copyAllFields(payload)), add explicit exclusion for title.

4) Update TypeScript/Flow/prop-types definitions and client models:
   - Remove title from response interfaces/types so response types reflect the new public API shape (only name for label).
   - Ensure request payload types do not include title; update create/update input types accordingly.
   - Add comments in types to state: "title removed from API responses; do not include title in requests (422)."

5) Update tests, fixtures, and mocks:
   - Update unit and integration tests that expected title in responses or used title fallback; change assertions to use name only.
   - Update mock server fixtures and storybook stories to remove title keys from response JSON and ensure mocks match the new contract.
   - Update any test fixtures used for form submissions so they do not include title in outgoing payloads.

6) E2E and manual verification:
   - Add/modify an end-to-end test that visits a listing/detail where entries were previously relying on title fallback and assert the UI renders correctly using name only.
   - In a local or staging run, use the browser devtools Network tab to verify:
     - Responses from the server no longer contain a "title" key in any entry object.
     - Outbound POST/PUT/PATCH request bodies DO NOT contain a "title" key.
     - If a request includes a title (manual test), the API responds with 422 as documented — this verifies the constraint; ensure the frontend never generates such requests.

7) Update storybook and developer docs:
   - Update component stories and README/docs to describe that the label field is name and title is no longer present in responses. Note the 422 constraint for outgoing title fields.

8) Add static checks (optional but recommended):
   - Add a unit test or lint rule that fails if code serializes an object containing the key "title" into API payloads (e.g., a small assertion in serializer tests that ensures title is not present).
   - Update TypeScript strictness (if applicable) so that response types without title cause compile errors where code still references title.

9) PR checklist for review:
   - All occurrences of reading title as fallback removed and replaced with name-only logic.
   - No code sends a "title" field in any request payload (search result assertion in PR description).
   - Type definitions updated to remove title from response types and request types.
   - All unit/integration/e2e tests and storybook fixtures updated and passing locally.
   - Manual verification documented: screenshots or steps proving network responses lack title and requests lack title.
   - Add a short note in the PR description documenting the preserved API facts: responses removed title, requests with title return 422, db columns unchanged, description/id/owner_id/created_at unchanged.

Acceptance criteria (must be true before merge/deploy):
- UI components only read and display name for labels; no component reads title.
- No outgoing API request contains a title key (verified by automated tests and by inspecting network traffic in a staging run).
- Mocks, stories, and tests updated to the new response shape (no title present).
- Unit and integration tests pass; e2e test demonstrates expected UI behavior with name-only responses.
- Documentation/PR message explicitly states: requests with title return 422; database fields are unchanged; description/id/owner_id/created_at remain available and unchanged.

Developer notes and gotchas:
- Do not change any backend or DB code. Treat title as removed from the public response surface, but the DB column name remains unchanged — do not attempt to map to or rename database fields in the frontend.
- Avoid introducing any temporary code that re-introduces title into requests (for backwards compatibility). Any such compatibility layer would produce 422s and break clients — do not implement.
- If you find code that conditionally sends title only for internal/debug endpoints, explicitly remove that behavior or gate it behind a development-only flag, ensuring production never sends title.

Minimal example code changes (illustrative patterns):
- Response consumption: replace
    // bad
    const label = item.name || item.title;
  with
    // good
    const label = item.name || '(no name)';

- Request serialization: replace
    const payload = { name: state.name, title: state.title, description: state.description };
    api.post('/entries', payload);
  with
    const payload = { name: state.name, description: state.description };
    api.post('/entries', payload);
  or explicitly remove title before send:
    delete payload.title;

Execution checklist to run before merging and deploying:
- Run full test suite (unit + integration + e2e).
- Inspect network traffic in a local/staging environment to confirm responses have no title and requests do not include title.
- Update PR description with a short verification log showing search results for title occurrences after changes.

Do not guess unrelated or unspecified server-side changes or timelines. If any ambiguity remains about when the backend will stop returning title, confirm with the backend team, then run the above verification against their staging API. The frontend implementation must assume:
- Public responses will not include title (use name only).
- Sending title in requests yields 422 (so frontend must never send title).

End of instructions.
